text:
raj: Hey team — noticing short (200-500ms) latency pulses on local small-block IO on a subset of nodes in us-west2. This is spiking GPU provisioning latency for <50ms jobs. Seen this on 4/10 nodes over the last 2 hours. log excerpt: `iostat -x 1 3` shows %util jump to 95 for nvme2 for ~2s. Any ideas?

sasha: I saw one of those earlier, looked like many tiny 4k writes from prefetch/sidecar caches. Not sure if it's ephemeral cleaner or a firmware hiccup.

maria: Can you paste the `dmesg` around the time? small-block pulses usually from writeback bursts or small fsync storms. Also: what kernel/driver?

raj: kernel 5.15.92, nvmf driver v1.3. dmesg snippet from one node: `nvme0: I/O 0x3e7b timed out`, then `nvme0: queue resume` and then a flood of `blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 2048`. But errors aren't permanent — device recovers.

infra-bot: ALERT: storage-latency-pulse detected on instance-52, instance-89, instance-114 in us-west2. Severity: medium. Autoretry engaged.

leo: Could be transient power-management/thermal throttling on that hardware revision. We had that one SKU where PM kicks in on short sustained small-block workloads. If it's the same SKU it explains the short recovery pattern.

raj: Good call. sku list: gnode-14b and gnode-14c affected. sku-14c had a firmware rollout last month.

sasha: Quick repro: run `fio --name=4k-burst --rw=randwrite --bs=4k --iodepth=64 --numjobs=4 --size=1G --time_based --runtime=60` on the node and watch `iostat`/`nvme monitor`. I can trigger a pulse in ~30s on 14c.

maria: For immediate mitigation: set `vm.dirty_ratio` lower and reduce background writeback with `echo 10 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio` (temp) and throttle the sidecar cache writes (we can add a backoff). That should flatten the bursts while we investigate firmware.

leo: Ops plan: 1) Quarantine sku-14c from new GPU provisioning (scale down in pool) 2) Rollback firmware on 14c candidates where possible 3) Run extended fio + spectral telemetry to capture pulses 4) Patch sidecar to coalesce small writes.

raj: I'll open the incident ticket and add the nodes + logs. Can someone take item 1? Preferably infra oncall. Also please don't do mass reboots yet — device recovers and rebooting could evict NVMe alignment metrics.

sasha: I'll take quarantine step and start fio runs on remaining pool. tagging @oncall.

maria: I'll draft a short KB with the temporary `dirty_ratio` tweak and the fio repro so support can use it.

raj: Thanks — update in the incident when you have quarantine done. :thumbsup:
